876fe7cb31.q: What are the most memorable aspects of a career spanning multiple construction disciplines and roles?
876fe7cb31.a: The fond memories are just the mateship within construction, the characters I've met along the way. The highlight was definitely going from job to job, meeting characters, good people, and helping people. Ray also mentions serious injuries on sites as lowlights, including pump blockages causing major incidents with broken bones and collapses, though the camaraderie amongst workers during emergencies was nothing short of amazing.

155e4ed48f.q: How does union administration and regulatory oversight affect industry culture and worker protection?
155e4ed48f.a: Ray states: I honestly don't think so about the current administration changing industry culture. He argues that the overreach of government with Mr Irving's administration is a national disgrace, similar to the parameters of the ABCC, where murderers and rapists had more rights than construction workers. He believes the union must protect members when money is floating around, but that government only wants monuments to justify their time in power and doesn't take responsibility for what happens on their watch.

890e4900a4.q: What is the trajectory of the union's role and influence in Australia's construction sector long-term?
890e4900a4.a: Ray believes the industry is still in a very strong position and that anyone thinking they will deregister the organisation and pull the timbers from under it should dream on, because for as long as there are people doing what they do, there's most certainly a role for the unions to play. He expresses frustration that unions deal with problems, fatalities, injuries, and rip-offs while being blamed.

1a9d37452b.q: What career path led Ray 'Rowdy' Smith from music industry management to construction work?
1a9d37452b.a: Ray spent nearly 30 years in the music industry, leaving school around 1975-1976, working as a roadie carrying black boxes and eventually becoming a manager. His father played drums and was interested in music and bands. Ray was determined to play in a band and be part of the industry, and went on to manage Johnny Diesel and the Injectors, who achieved major success, becoming the first band in Australia to sell half a million copies. He transitioned to construction after leaving the music touring circuit.

8a98a9d4c8.q: What was the scale of success achieved by Johnny Diesel and the Injectors in the Australian music market?
8a98a9d4c8.a: Johnny Diesel and the Injectors were the first band in Australia to sell half a million copies, holding that title for a few years until John Farnham's The Voice superseded them with higher sales. The band secured a record deal from America in 1998, and Ray along with the band lived in Memphis, Tennessee for about 8 months where they recorded their first album.

62bbb8bacc.q: How did Ray Smith manage high-profile touring artists and what challenges did he encounter?
62bbb8bacc.a: Ray toured with major international acts including the Rolling Stones and Joe Cocker, becoming good friends with Cocker who would ring him whenever he toured Australia. Ray was Oasis's Australian tour manager during their early tour, and had to manage a Gallagher brother who was disruptive at Sydney Entertainment Centre. Ray ultimately decided to leave touring because of the constant airports, tour buses, planes, trains, and everything in between, which took him a long time to recover from.

d4c279c2e9.q: What approach did Ray Smith take when confronted with disrespectful behavior from a touring artist?
d4c279c2e9.a: When a Gallagher brother from Oasis was carrying on rudely at Sydney Entertainment Centre about the third night of their tour, Ray politely bumped him into a room and said: if we're going to work together, you're going to learn to be a bit more respectful in the way you talk to people. I don't know how you talk to your old man, but you won't be talking to me like that. The artist's London management later praised Ray for being the first to pull the artist in line, and the next day the artist apologized.

2f86a24ead.q: How did a music industry professional transition into construction labouring in 2004?
2f86a24ead.a: Ray Smith finished his previous life in the music industry and rang Steve Longy asking if it was possible to give him a job as a labourer, suggesting he just needed a break for about 12 months. Longy agreed, and in January 2004, Smith's first job in the industry was at Coot Island doing the old redevelopment, working for a company called Ruleway as a TA.

372a66ded6.q: What contamination issues were encountered on the Coot Island redevelopment project?
372a66ded6.a: The site contained PFAS chemical residue from a historical fire, which had leached into the subsoil and persists to this day. The groundworks revealed castigens and nasties that were buried on the site, and the contamination was so significant that it later impacted the Westgate project.

831778c87c.q: What safety incident occurred during night shift work on an active railway bridge construction?
831778c87c.a: During the Long Walk railway bridge project, there was a night when the overhead power lines for the trains were supposed to be turned off but weren't, leaving the live lines energized while workers in scissor lifts were operating between them. The union health and safety crew intervened to prevent catastrophe, but it was described as a very hairy night and catastrophe averted.

cedd21aa0a.q: What unusual item was discovered embedded in a concrete deck pour on the Long Walk bridge?
cedd21aa0a.a: A banana skin had been left in one of the deck pours during concreting, and years later Ray Smith and his mate Chuckles found the imprint of the banana still visible on the bridge, suggesting the banana had never been removed before the concrete was finished.

929cf8c77e.q: How long did workers spend on road patching work on the Eastlink project?
929cf8c77e.a: Ray Smith and his mate Ed patched approximately 30 kilometres of Eastlink over a period of a few years working with Clifton. They were subbed out to contractors like Hollands or Fiesa and given a ute with their gear to work their way through the patching sections.

439c6a00fb.q: What injury recording practices did contractors try to enforce on the Eastlink project?
439c6a00fb.a: Contractors attempted to not record any injuries on the Eastlink project and intimidated local doctors when workers went to get medical certificates. They also used a 'lost time' injury recording system and refused to acknowledge workers who needed to live away from home, avoiding payment of living away from home allowances.

483f5d6e7e.q: What union agreements governed work conditions on the Eastlink project?
483f5d6e7e.a: The Eastlink project was initially covered by an AWU agreement, but when that agreement ran out, it was replaced by a CFMEU agreement, at which point working conditions improved significantly. Bill Shorten was the Secretary of the AWU at the time, and John Cummins as President intervened in the agreement negotiations.

e2d69ce0f4.q: What safety concern arose during railway station upgrade work at Nunna Wadding?
e2d69ce0f4.a: At Nunna Wadding station, approximately 40 workers were trying to work in an area of only 10 to 20 square metres, which Ray Smith identified as a disaster waiting to happen. When he raised concerns about the dangerously crowded workspace, management dismissed his safety worries.

a613adc844.q: What workplace facilities issue did a union delegate address on the Heatherhill Road overpass section of Eastlink?
a613adc844.a: Ray Smith stopped the job when he discovered there were no women's toilets despite numerous women members of the CFMEU working in traffic management and other roles on the Heatherhill Road overpass. The project manager, an ex-Leighton's person, initially resisted but the problem was solved after approximately one day.

7597e70f5a.q: How did different contractor management styles affect worker conditions on the Eastlink project?
7597e70f5a.a: Leighton's were better organized and actually helped their subbies with safety and production, whereas when Thies were in control or John Hollands were in control, there were significantly more problems. With Thies, productivity came first and safety was a distant second, making it a daily battle for delegates to maintain safe working conditions.

1f40144765.q: What was the significance of school construction projects during the global financial crisis period?
1f40144765.a: Following the 2008 global financial crisis, government funding for school construction packages helped keep the construction industry and workers employed. These school packages included new halls and playground upgrades that schools desperately needed, representing a proper use of government funds despite Ray Smith's general skepticism of Labor governments.
